title: How to Train Your Dragon
tagline: Fish for the dragon, stew for the Vikings.
about: A young Viking who can't fight befriends the dragon he was meant to kill.
cue: Serve the fish bites when Hiccup offers Toothless a fish.

    StartersToothless's fish bitesPanko crumbed white fish strips with a lemon dill yoghurt dipHow to make it500g white fish fillets50g plain flour2 eggs120g panko breadcrumbs200g Greek yoghurt1 lemon1 bunch dill2 L vegetable oilCut the white fish fillets into strips.Dip in the flour, the beaten eggs and the panko, and fry in the vegetable oil at 180°C for 3 minutes until golden.Mix the Greek yoghurt with lemon and chopped dill and serve with lemon wedges.Gobber's smoked sausagesCharred smoked sausage chunks with wholegrain mustardHow to make it600g smoked sausages4 tbsp wholegrain mustardCook the thick smoked sausages over high heat for 8 minutes, turning, until charred and split.Cut into chunks and serve on a board with the wholegrain mustard for dipping.Stoick's pan bread with honey butterStoick the Vast's table in the Great HallHow to make itAs written, serves 4Crusty seeded bread baked in a blazing hot pan, torn at the table and slathered with whipped honey and sea salt butter.Mix 500g bread flour, 7g yeast, 10g salt, 2 tbsp mixed seeds and 350ml warm water and knead 8 minutes.Rest 1 hour.Shape into a round and put in an oiled 26cm ovenproof frying pan, slash the top, brush with water and scatter more seeds.Rest 30 minutes.Bake at 230°C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow.Beat 125g soft butter with 2 tbsp honey and flaky salt and serve with the warm bread.MainsViking lamb stewLamb shoulder, carrot, parsnip and pearl barley in beef stockHow to make it1kg lamb shoulder1 onion3 carrots2 parsnips100g pearl barley1 bunch thyme1.3 L beef stockBrown the diced lamb shoulder, then add the onion, the carrots and the parsnips in chunks, the pearl barley, thyme and the beef stock.Cover and simmer 2 hours until the lamb is tender and the barley is plump.Serve in big bowls with bread.Night Fury fire-roasted chicken legsToothless lighting up the sky over BerkHow to make itAs written, serves 4Chicken marylands rubbed with smoked paprika, garlic and rosemary, roasted until charred, then lacquered with smoky honey and served with roast carrots.Heat the oven to 200°C.Rub 4 chicken marylands with 2 tbsp oil, 2 tsp smoked paprika, 2 crushed garlic cloves, chopped rosemary and salt.Roast on a tray with 6 halved carrots for 40 minutes.Warm 3 tbsp honey with half a tsp smoked paprika and 1 tbsp cider vinegar.Brush over the chicken and roast 10 minutes more until sticky and charred at the edges.Rest 5 minutes and spoon the pan juices over.SweetsHoney cakesSoft cinnamon cakes baked in muffin cases and brushed with warm honeyHow to make it125g butter170g honey2 eggs200g self-raising flour1 tsp ground cinnamon80ml milkBeat the butter with the honey, add the eggs, then fold in the self-raising flour, the cinnamon and the milk.Spoon into muffin cases and bake at 175°C for 18 minutes.Brush with the warm honey while hot.DrinksBerk hot spiced berry punchApple juice simmered with berries, cinnamon, star anise and orangeHow to make it300g frozen mixed berries1 L cloudy apple juice1 cinnamon stick1 star anise1 orange1 tbsp honey1 punnet blueberriesPut the frozen mixed berries, the cloudy apple juice, the cinnamon stick, the star anise, the strips of orange peel and the honey in a saucepan.Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 10 minutes, pressing the berries.Strain through a sieve into a jug.Pour into mugs and drop in a few fresh blueberries.Serve hot, or chill and pour over ice in summer.
